classification.difficultyReason: Infer the overlap from two set totals and the number outside both sets, then calculate probabilities from individual regions.

content.prompt: In a youth club of 50 people, 18 play basketball, 28 play soccer and 10 play neither sport.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Represent this information on a Venn diagram.

answer.short: Let $B$ represent basketball and $S$ represent soccer. Basketball only: 12; both: 6; soccer only: 22; neither: 10.
answer.worked:
Let $B$ represent basketball and $S$ represent soccer. There are $50-10=40$ people who play at least one sport.
$$\begin{align*}|B\cap S|&=18+28-40\\|B\cap S|&=6\end{align*}$$
Basketball only: $18-6=12$.

Soccer only: $28-6=22$.

Place 12, 6 and 22 in the basketball-only, overlap and soccer-only regions respectively, and 10 outside both circles.
